commands.name: init
commands.summary: Write a starter configuration file
commands.description: init writes a starter better-compute.config.ts (or the JavaScript form when --config names a .mjs or .js file): a configuration factory that uses PGlite in a local .better-compute-pglite directory for development and PostgreSQL when BETTER_COMPUTE_DATABASE_URL is set, reads the secret and base URL from the environment, shows where better-iam plugs in, and exports an empty list of project commands. It never overwrites an existing file.
commands.usage: better-compute init [--config better-compute.config.ts]

flags.description: Where to write the configuration (.ts, .mts, .js or .mjs)

commands.name: migrate
commands.summary: Create or upgrade the database schema and apply module migrations
commands.description: migrate runs compute.initialize(): it checks every method's IAM action against the merged catalog and the normative method table (INVALID_CONFIG on a mismatch), then creates or upgrades the compute schema and applies every module's and plugin's migrations. Run it on every deploy before the application starts; it is idempotent.
commands.usage: better-compute migrate [--config PATH]

flags.description: Configuration module; default: the nearest better-compute.config.{mjs,js,ts,mts}

commands.name: doctor
commands.summary: Check the database, schema, clock, method registry and IAM wiring
commands.description: doctor runs compute.selfCheck() (applied migrations, btree_gist, compute_now() against the database clock, the method → action registry, and each module's own checks) and adds the CLI's findings, such as a deployment with no IAM configured, the PKI bundle, and the configuration's host export (whether the gateway role can authenticate daemons by node certificate, reach the api's pokes, tunnels and revocations, and whether host routes fit beside the API). It only reads. --strict exits non-zero (DOCTOR_FINDINGS) when any error or warning is found.
commands.usage: better-compute doctor [--strict] [--pki PATH] [--config PATH]

commands.name: version
commands.summary: Print the better-compute version
commands.description: version prints the version of this command line (also --version or -v).
commands.usage: better-compute version

commands.name: serve
commands.summary: Run the API and the workers in this process
commands.description: serve loads the configuration, migrates (skip with --no-migrate once a deploy step runs better-compute migrate), starts the worker roles (controllers: reconcilers and the command sweeper; scheduler; sinks: outbox dispatch; iam: IAM jobs) under their leases, and serves the API with compute.nodeHandler on --host:--port. Run several processes against one database: leases and shard ownership keep each job single-writer. --roles api serves the API only; --roles controllers,sinks runs a worker with no listener; --roles gateway runs the daemon gateway over mTLS from the configuration's host.gateway (all includes it when configured), with the report hooks of the built-in modules and tunnels when the deployment issues exec tickets. Beside the API the listener answers /healthz, /readyz, /.well-known/better-compute (the server's document, with JoinService's public keys when pki.join publishes them: the fallback bcd checks against its pins) and the host export's own routes (for example GET /watch and GET /metrics). SIGINT or SIGTERM drains the gateway first, then stops the listener and the workers, releasing their leases.
commands.usage: better-compute serve [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--roles ROLES] [--no-migrate] [--config PATH]

flags.description: The address to listen on
The port to listen on (0 picks a free one)
all, or a comma list of api, gateway and controllers, scheduler, sinks, iam
Do not run migrations first

commands.name: dev
commands.summary: Run a local development server with no setup
commands.description: dev runs the API and every worker role on 127.0.0.1. With a configuration file (or BETTER_COMPUTE_DATABASE_URL) it uses that deployment; without one it keeps PGlite in --data (default .better-compute/dev-db; --memory for a throwaway database) and a generated deployment secret in .better-compute/dev-secret (owner-only), so repeated runs keep their data. It always migrates first. Without IAM configured only public methods answer; see better-compute iam setup. --sim N adds a gateway on loopback cleartext HTTP/2 (sessions authenticate by a header; local development only) and N simulated machines that join the way bcd does: a join token sealed to throwaway dev JoinService keys, the Join RPC, a Session stream, diag.nvml acceptance and adoption by the real runtime. Without configured IAM, --sim starts an embedded in-memory better-iam and prints its root token; with configured IAM it acts as BETTER_COMPUTE_TOKEN, which must be a root administrator.
commands.usage: better-compute dev [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--data DIR] [--memory] [--sim N] [--sim-variant VARIANT] [--config PATH]

commands.name: sim
commands.summary: Run the deterministic fleet simulator and check its invariants
commands.description: sim runs --nodes FakeDaemons on fake hardware against the in-memory gateway stub for --duration of simulated time, with a steady workload (diagnostics, inventory refreshes, log collection, reboots, GPU bookings) and --chaos faults (none, light, heavy: crashes, reboots, journal loss, partitions, half-open links, resets, stalls, gateway kills), then quiesces for --settle and checks invariants I1 (no double booking), I2 (at-most-once side effects), I5 (no allocation released only because its node disconnected) and I8 (usage). Nothing reads the wall clock: the same --seed prints the same digest. It exits SIM_INVARIANT_VIOLATED when an invariant fails. Needs @better-compute/testing.
commands.usage: better-compute sim [--seed SEED] [--nodes N] [--duration DURATION] [--settle DURATION] [--chaos LEVEL] [--log PATH]

commands.name: pki init
commands.summary: Create the machine PKI: root, node, serving and internal CAs and the JoinService keys
commands.description: pki init creates a deployment's machine PKI (PLAN.md §13) and writes it to one JSON file with mode 0600: an offline root CA, the per-region node CA (agent client certificates), the gateway serving CA, the internal control-plane CA, and the JoinService signing and encryption keys. No key does two jobs. The private keys are sealed with AES-256-GCM under a key derived from BETTER_COMPUTE_SECRET; without the secret, pass --plaintext to store them as PEM instead. --offline-root writes the root key to its own file and leaves it out of the bundle: keep that file off the servers. It prints the pins install scripts need (the same as pki show) and never overwrites an existing file.

commands.name: pki rotate-command-root
commands.summary: Rotate the command-signing root in three steps: add, switch, drop
commands.description: pki rotate-command-root performs one step of a command-signing root rotation (PLAN.md §13) on the bundle and writes it back (sealed with BETTER_COMPUTE_SECRET when set). --stage add creates a new root and publishes it beside the current one (the trust bundle's version goes up); workers keep signing under the current root. Roll the bundle out to every process: daemons receive the new version in Welcome.trust. --stage switch, once every daemon holds that version, makes workers sign under the new root while the old one stays trusted. --stage drop, at least 24 hours later (worker keys live at most 24 h), removes the old root (version up again). Each step prints the roots and version daemons will trust.
commands.usage: better-compute pki rotate-command-root --stage STAGE [--pki PATH]

commands.name: daemon install-script
commands.summary: Write the POSIX sh script that installs bcd on a server and joins it to a pool
commands.description: daemon install-script emits the bcd installer (PLAN.md §3.3, §6). The script reads the join token only from BCD_JOIN_TOKEN or standard input, downloads the pinned bcd for the machine's architecture from {base-url}{base-path}/downloads/bcd/{version}/linux-{arch}, checks it against --sha256 (or the digests of a --release-manifest verified here under --release-pins, product bcd, version --bcd-version), installs /usr/local/bin/bcd, /etc/bcd/config.toml (mode 0600: gateway URL, site and the serving CA, join signing and join encryption key pins, in bcd's sha256/<base64> form), the JoinService encryption key, and a hardened bcd.service, then runs bcd join and starts the service. Run on a configured host without a token, it upgrades bcd in place. The pins come from the PKI bundle's public half (pki init), so no secret is needed. The script holds no secret either: create the join token separately (joinTokens.create) and hand it over out of band.
commands.usage: better-compute daemon install-script --pool ID --site ID --gateway-url URL --base-url URL [--base-path PATH] --bcd-version VERSION [--sha256 ARCH=HEX,…] [--release-manifest PATH] [--release-pins PINS] [--release-threshold N] [--pki PATH] [--out PATH]

commands.name: iam setup
commands.summary: Print the example compute policies and create the root billing meters in better-iam
commands.description: iam setup prints the PLAN.md §12.6 example policies, gpu-user and agent-guardrails, for an organization administrator to apply: compute cannot write organization policies. The policies are parameterized by the session JWT audience (the compute API's URL), the GPU model, regions and limits of the bounded-reservation statement. With --meters it also creates the §12.7 root meters in better-iam: one gpu.<model>.hours per GPU model family, plus node.metal.hours, vps.vcpu.hours and vps.memory.gib.hours. Meters that already exist are left alone, so re-running is safe. It sets no prices: pricing is an operator decision (billing.setPrice).

commands.name: release sign

commands.description: release sign hashes every file in DIR (not subdirectories; *.sha256, manifest.json and signature files are skipped), derives each artifact's platform from goreleaser names (_linux_amd64.), and writes a manifest signed with --key. --sequence must increase with every release of --product: installers and bcd refuse a manifest whose sequence is below the last one they accepted. commands.name: support bundle
commands.summary: Write a redacted diagnostics bundle for a support request
commands.description: support bundle collects what a support request about the control plane needs: the CLI, Node and platform versions; the configuration's shape (database kind, modules, whether IAM, PKI, tunnels and a notifier are configured; never URLs or values); doctor's findings; applied migrations; gateway and worker heartbeats; work-queue, command and IAM-inbox backlogs; and node counts by state. Environment variables appear by name only. Before anything is written, the bundle is scanned for join tokens (bcjt_), IAM tokens (biam_), JWTs, private keys, URL passwords and the deployment's own secrets, and each is replaced; a bundle in which a secret survives is refused (SUPPORT_BUNDLE_LEAK). The file is written owner-only. It only reads.
commands.usage: better-compute support bundle [--out PATH] [--pki PATH] [--config PATH]
